newsitem.title: CHINA: LUJIAZUI BLAMES SUBSIDIARY FOR H1 FALL.
newsitem.headline: LUJIAZUI BLAMES SUBSIDIARY FOR H1 FALL.

text.p: Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development Co Ltd, a key hard currency B share firm listed in Shanghai, said on Monday its poor net profit in the first half of 1997 was partly due to losses by a subsidiary.

The subsidiary, Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade United Development Co Ltd, in which the listed firm holds a 55 percent stake, made a loss on the return of a piece of land it had sold, a company official told Reuters.
He said the buyer had to transfer the project originally planned for the site elsewhere.
Lujiazui, based on China's premier development area of Pudong, east of Shanghai's Huangpu River, booked a loss of 67.9 million yuan for the subsidiary due to the cancelled sale, the official said.
The firm on Friday posted a net profit of 179.376 million yuan for the first half of 1997, down sharply from 548.959 million yuan in the first half of 1996.
The net profit represented only 28.47 percent of the company's target of 630 million yuan net for the whole of 1997.
Despite the poor performance in the first half, brokers said the company's prospects were still good for this and the next few years.
One Shanghai-based foreign broker said the firm's land banks had held their value due to the fast development of Pudong.
In addition, the company had not booked income from some land sales, which might be reflected in the 1997 results as well as for the next few years, one local broker said.
